term: reception of esse versus external cause of esse
resolution: De ente c.3 joins two things in 'recipit aliquid ab alio': an origin from another (an external efficient cause of esse, DEF-Q3A4-EXTERNAL-ESSE-CAUSE-MODEL) and reception in a principle that stands as potency to the received act (DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN). SUBSISTENT-INFINITY-FROM-RECEPTION uses only reception in a principle; no step infers reception from having an external cause or the converse. Reception of esse is also not reception of a form in matter: q.7 a.2 lets a subsistent created form be unreceived in matter while its esse is received. A third case is left open: a subsisting form communicating its esse to matter (ST I q.76 a.1 ad 5, 'esse in quo ipsa subsistit, communicat materiae corporali'; SCG II.80 n.13, the body as 'subiectum ipsum recipiens' of the united soul's esse). This record does not decide whether that communication is EsseReceivedIn. If it is, the body receives the soul's esse without being its essence, and STMT-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN-OWN-ESSENCE is attacked (REL-UNITED-SOUL-ESSE-RECEIVED-BY-BODY-ATTACKS-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN-OWN-ESSENCE). If it is not, the premise is unaffected, but only because of that distinction, which no source read here states.
